findings.issue: normalizeStyleRanges does not reject offsets that are not finite numbers. With start NaN, Math.max(0, Math.min(NaN, n)) is NaN, and `start >= end` is false, so the entry is kept. NaN then goes into `points` and the sort, and a range with a NaN offset can come back out. sanitizeStyleRanges guards with Number.isInteger, but newTextElement passes caller-supplied opts.styleRanges straight to normalizeStyleRanges, and fractional offsets also get through to slice/startsWith. Confidence: high (the arithmetic is deterministic).
findings.fix: In the loop, skip any entry whose start or end is not Number.isFinite, and truncate the rest with Math.trunc before clamping, so every path gets the same guarantees as sanitizeStyleRanges.

findings.issue: getTextStyleRunLayout measures each prefix twice. The prefixWidth of run n+1 is the same as the runEndWidth of run n, so it calls getLineWidth (measureText) 2 x runs + 1 times per line where runs + 1 would do. It runs on every canvas cache miss and every SVG export.
findings.fix: Keep the previous runEndWidth in a variable (it starts at 0 for offset 0) and use it as the next run's prefixWidth. Only measure line.slice(0, nextOffset) for each run.

findings.issue: Imports newTextElement from the "@excalidraw/element" barrel. change_plan.md (Conventions, Decision 'How other packages import') says code inside packages/element imports relatively, and the file already imports every other symbol from ../src/*.
findings.fix: Change it to `import { newTextElement } from "../src/newElement";` and put it in the relative-import group.

findings.issue: The case 'survives a bound-text container's wrapping' never binds the text to the container (the rectangle has no boundElements). It also wraps with the fixed 10px `font` instead of getFontString(text), so the wrap is not the one the bound text actually renders with. It checks getStyleRunsForLines on an arbitrary wrap, not the bound-text layout.
findings.fix: Build the wrap with getFontString(text) (or create the text with fontSize 10), and bind it (container boundElements plus text containerId, e.g. through API.createElement with a label) so getBoundTextMaxWidth reflects a real container.

findings.issue: The caret case uses caret 2 where the plan says caret 1. The code is right: caret 1 means the 'a' was inserted at offset 0, which is the range's start edge, so the result is [{1,3}], not [{0,3}]. The plan's expectation broke its own edge rule. That leaves the 'insert at the start edge' caret case untested.
findings.fix: Add an assertion that shiftStyleRangesForEdit(aa, "aa", "aaa", 1) equals [{ start: 1, end: 3, strokeColor: red }], so all three caret positions are pinned.
